name: relay
title: An outbound relay
summary: A server that sends mail for applications and other servers and holds no mailbox anybody reads. IMAP and POP3 are closed, an address that bounces hard is suppressed and the sender told at once, deliveries back off from a destination that asks them to and never hold more than ten sessions open to one, and every delivery attempt is traced and kept for three months, because a relay is asked about what it sent long after it sent it.
steps: Decide who may relay: that is an IP range's question - require authentication on the range the senders connect from, or name their addresses - and a profile does not answer it.
Switch DKIM signing and its key rotation on for each sending domain: both are the domain's, and the server has no value of them to set.
Set the sending limits per account in [SendingLimits] if the senders are to be held to a volume: those keys are the settings file's, not the store's.

entries.name: protocolimap
entries.why: nobody reads mail on a relay, and a listener nobody uses is one more to attack

entries.name: protocolpop3
entries.why: the same for POP3

entries.name: authallowplaintext
entries.why: a sender's password is never taken over a connection without TLS

entries.name: AutoBanOnLogonFailureEnabled
entries.why: an address that guesses a relay's passwords is shut out

entries.name: CreateDefaultSpecialUseFolders
entries.why: an account here is a sender's credential, not a mailbox

entries.name: DirectoryEnabled
entries.why: the accounts are applications, not a directory of people to list to each other

entries.name: BounceProcessingEnabled
entries.why: an address that bounces hard is not written to again

entries.name: BounceHardBounceThreshold
entries.why: one hard bounce is enough: the receiver has said the address does not exist

entries.name: BounceSuppressionAction
entries.why: refuse: a submission to a suppressed address is refused at RCPT with the reason, so the application learns it at once

entries.name: BounceSuppressionExpiryDays
entries.why: a suppressed address gets another chance after six months

entries.name: BounceReadDeliveryReports
entries.why: the reports receivers send back are matched to what was sent

entries.name: OutboundBackoffMaxMinutes
entries.why: the longest a destination that keeps asking to slow down is left alone, as shipped

entries.name: OutboundBackoffMinutes
entries.why: a destination that answers a slow-down reply is left alone for two minutes, doubling, as shipped

entries.name: MaxOutboundConnsPerDestination
entries.why: no destination is held more than ten sessions at once, which is what large providers tolerate

entries.name: maxdelivertythreads
entries.why: a relay's work is delivery, so more of it runs at once

entries.name: smtpnoofretries
entries.why: a destination that is down for an afternoon still gets its mail

entries.name: smtpminutesbetweenretries
entries.why: an hour between attempts, as shipped, so twelve of them span half a day

entries.name: QuickRetries
entries.why: a delivery that failed for a moment is tried again within minutes before the hourly schedule

entries.name: SmtpDeliveryConnectionSecurity
entries.why: STARTTLS whenever the destination offers it, as shipped

entries.name: VerifyRemoteSslCertificate
entries.why: a destination's certificate is checked, so that a policy that requires TLS means it

entries.name: MtaStsEnabled
entries.why: a recipient domain that publishes an MTA-STS policy gets TLS to a verified host, or no delivery

entries.name: DaneEnforcementEnabled
entries.why: a recipient domain that publishes TLSA records is held to them

entries.name: MessageTraceEnabled
entries.why: every delivery attempt is recorded, which is what answers whether a message went

entries.name: MessageTraceRetentionDays
entries.why: three months of it rather than the thirty days shipped, because a relay is asked about old sends

entries.name: ReputationWatchEnabled
entries.why: a relay whose address is on a block list stops getting its mail through, and you are told
